title: Gujarati Store Owner Shot Dead During Armed Robbery in Tennessee
excerpt: Suresh Patel, 56, from Mehsana was killed at his Jackson liquor store while his 19-year-old daughter witnessed the attack; the masked suspect remains at large.
body:
• Suresh Patel, 56, from Gujarat's Mehsana district, was shot dead during an armed robbery at his liquor store in Jackson, Tennessee on the evening of August 20.
  • Patel's 19-year-old daughter was present in the store during the attack but escaped without physical injury.
  • The masked suspect fled in a white sedan and remains at large; Jackson Police have released a description and are urging the public to come forward.
  • The killing adds to a pattern of violent crimes targeting Indian-origin store owners across the United States.

A 56-year-old Indian-origin store owner from Gujarat was shot dead during an armed robbery at his business in Jackson, Tennessee last Thursday evening, with his teenage daughter witnessing the attack.

Suresh Patel, originally from Mehsana district in Gujarat, was working at Ridgecrest Cellars Wine and Spirits on Ridgecrest Road when a masked gunman entered the store at approximately 9 p.m. on August 20, according to the Jackson Police Department.

The Shooting

Officers said the suspect entered the store, displayed a weapon, and demanded money from employees. After taking cash from the business, the gunman fired multiple shots, striking Patel. Despite the response of emergency medical personnel, Patel was pronounced dead at the scene.

Patel's 19-year-old daughter was also present at the store during the robbery. She escaped without physical injury, though the psychological trauma of witnessing her father's killing cannot be measured.

Suspect at Large

Police described the suspect as a male wearing a gray hoodie, jeans, and black work-style boots. His face was covered by a paintball-style mask. Investigators said he fled the scene in a white sedan.

Authorities are urging anyone who may have witnessed the robbery, seen the suspect or vehicle, or has information that could help identify the person responsible to contact the Jackson Police Department at 731-425-8400 or Crime Stoppers at 731-424-8477. Crime Stoppers callers may remain anonymous.

A Recurring Pattern

Patel's death adds to a grim and recurring pattern of violent crimes targeting Indian-origin business owners in the United States. Indian immigrants and their families have long operated convenience stores, gas stations, and liquor stores across the country — businesses that frequently become targets for armed robberies due to their cash-heavy operations and often limited security.

In May 2026, Meghnaben Patel, a 45-year-old woman from Gujarat, was shot dead during a robbery at a supermarket in Virginia where she had worked for a decade. In June 2025, Dasari Gopikrishna, 32, from Andhra Pradesh was fatally shot during a robbery at a convenience store in Dallas, Texas. In July 2025, Mandeep Singh, 36, was killed during an armed robbery at a food mart in Georgia.

These incidents have repeatedly raised concerns within the Indian-American community about the safety of small-business owners who are disproportionately vulnerable to violent crime.

Community in Mourning

Patel's death has left his family and the local community reeling. He is remembered by those who knew him as a hardworking store employee whose life was cut short by senseless violence. The investigation remains ongoing as police work to identify and apprehend the suspect.

The Indian consulate has not yet issued a statement regarding the incident. Community members in Jackson and the broader Indian-American diaspora are mourning yet another loss to the cycle of violence that has claimed the lives of too many immigrant small-business owners.
nri_angle: The killing of a Gujarati store owner in Tennessee extends a pattern of violent crimes against Indian-origin small-business owners across the United States.
